summary: Destructor for an array of 3D sound source objects. When the array pointer (this+0x4) and the global dword_8AFE88 are both non-null, iterates the 132-byte-stride array destroying each non-null entry via F_3DSoundSourceDestructor, then walks the same entries backwards calling sub_4A2220 to clean internal state and frees the allocation block via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Finally zeroes both the pointer and the count fields (this+0x4, this+0x0).

local_names.array: pointer to the 132-byte-stride sound source array stored at this+0x4
local_names.count: number of array entries stored at this+0x0

operations.description: Proceeds only when the array pointer (this+0x4) is non-null and the global dword_8AFE88 is non-null; otherwise skips the whole teardown and jumps to zeroing the fields.
Iterates the array only while the count field (this+0x0) is greater than zero.
Walks the 132-byte-stride array from index 0 up to count; for each entry whose leading dword is non-null it destroys that sound source object.
Calls F_3DSoundSourceDestructor on each non-null entry dword of the 132-byte-stride array to destroy the individual 3D sound source object.
Walks the same 132-byte-stride entries backwards (from the header-derived count down to zero), calling sub_4A2220 on each entry to clean up its internal fields.
Calls sub_4A2220 on each array entry as part of the second, backwards cleanup pass.
Frees the allocation block that backs the array via FreeWrapper_7bcf; the block is addressed as the array pointer minus 4 (the element-count header).
Clears the array pointer field (this+0x4) to 0 and then the count field (this+0x0) to 0, leaving the container empty.
Returns the final result value (the zeroed count) to the caller.
